analysis.title: International Market Intelligence - Morning Briefing (November 9, 2026)
key_insights: APAC markets are higher after Friday's US gains, led by tech. Taiwan is the standout as the government steps up support. An NVDA board investigation pushes NDX into the red.
Trump said it is highly unlikely he will resume strikes on Iran. Scepticism persists over a negotiated outcome given the wide gap between the two sides.

The author sees midterms meaning three things for the market narrative: a flatter geopolitical risk curve in 2027, constraints on data centres, and greater fiscal discipline with some realignment toward the political centre. The author calls this positive for bonds and broadening.
Signs of capitulation suggest momentum longs will probably bounce soon, though this may be more of a risk-management exercise.
Thematic preference: SX7E (vs insurance), renewables, ACA subsidy-exposed names and hyperscalers, versus federal government contractors and staples.

Buyside capex expectations have clearly peaked, evidenced by lower valuation multiples. The sell-side will probably need to trim estimates somewhat. Capex can still grow YoY and the macro implications may be limited.

JPM's Dubravko notes the largest unwind of long momentum (vs market) in about 40 years, deleveraging metrics back at Liberation Day levels, and sentiment shifting from bullish in June to bearish now. He sees an intra-cycle reset and another deleveraging event in the AI supercycle, not end-cycle dynamics.

JPM Positioning Intelligence says selling has not yet signalled broad capitulation because the TPM buy signal has not triggered. It expects HF alpha to recover, as HF returns have often bounced after similar short-term drawdowns.

Exposure has reset in momentum (three-year low, near neutral) and AI themes (semis positioning back to early-2026 levels). US de-grossing is now below its seasonal average and gross flows have tended to move sideways from here.

The team is tactically bullish on global equities. The regional preference is long US and Asia (Japan, South Korea, Taiwan) versus EU. The US is overheating, Europe is recovering from stagflation, and Asia has pockets of both.
Broadening can come back, more clearly in US than EU. European earnings fundamentals are good and positioning gives a buy signal, but EU conviction needs stability in EGB spreads.

Longs: tech and supercycle themes across infrastructure (inference, semi cap), less-levered hyperscalers and AI-vulnerables (AI and application software). Also cyclicals with a secular tailwind (EU and JA banks, EU industrials, JA machinery, GE Infra, EU miners), EU pharma and UKX in low vol, and selectively consumer.
Shorts: AI-vulnerable names ex-software, short-cycle data center capex names, EU insurance, challenged industries (autos, chemicals, Asian consumer electronics, MedTech) and MDAX.
Option hedges: keep MCX below UKX until clarity emerges on spending, pragmatism and ideology, and short FR vs EU domestics on politics and dislocation.

Multi-Strat de-grossing was the largest 20-day event since Covid. L-S spreads improved over the past week, leaving 5-day alpha close to flat. After 20-day gross flows first fell below the 5th percentile (as on Oct. 27), alpha was higher over the next 20 days in 9 of 10 cases.

In past midterm election years the pattern most closely resembles 2022, when de-grossing continued into mid-month. Gross flows recovered in December in both years, alongside a market sell-off and substantial short additions.

Regional HF flows diverged. EMEA and China/HK saw net buying while North America and Japan saw net selling, with North America sharply de-grossed. European short covering hit an extreme 3z level, last seen in late 2022.

HF net leverage fell about 4% over the past week to near 12-month lows. Eq L/S net leverage is at a three-year low, while All Strategy net leverage is around the 40th percentile on three- and five-year bases. Semis were the most net-sold US theme, software flows were more neutral, and defensives ex-healthcare began to rebound.

risk_factors: Selling may continue if markets do not rebound, with CTAs neutral and so still able to sell.
Eq L/S alpha is still deteriorating, YTD returns are declining late in the year, and retail demand is soft.
The buyside capex peak means the sell-side will probably need to trim estimates.
Instability in EGB spreads limits conviction in European broadening.
The wide gap between the US and Iran leaves a negotiated outcome in doubt.
Past midterm years, 2022 in particular, saw de-grossing continue into mid-month and a December recovery coinciding with a market sell-off.
Upcoming market catalysts are likely to have a big impact on the path.
vol_and_positioning: JPM's Dubravko notes the largest unwind of long momentum (vs market) in about 40 years and deleveraging metrics back at Liberation Day levels.
The TPM buy signal has not triggered, so broad capitulation has not yet been signalled.
Global momentum exposure is near three-year lows and close to neutral. APAC momentum exposure also fell quickly from more extreme levels.
HF net leverage fell about 4% in a week to near 12-month lows. Eq L/S net leverage is at a three-year low. All Strategy net leverage is around the 40th percentile.

In the past five years HFs rebounded over the following 5 and 10 days in all eight comparable events where 5- and 20-day net returns fell below -2z. Late February 2020 and late October 2018 were followed by further losses.
European short covering reached an extreme 3z level, last seen in late 2022.

tension_points.bull_case: History suggests a rebound is more likely than not. Multi-Strat alpha rose after 9 of 10 past gross-flow troughs, HFs rebounded in all eight comparable drawdowns over the past five years, and momentum and semis exposure have reset.
tension_points.bear_case: Selling has not yet signalled broad capitulation because the TPM buy signal has not triggered. CTAs are neutral and could still sell, Eq L/S alpha is deteriorating, and late October 2018 and February 2020 were followed by further losses.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A further market sell-off without a rebound, since the report says a rebound in absolute HF returns may depend partly on the market.

tension_points.bull_case: European earnings fundamentals are good and positioning is giving a buy signal.
tension_points.bear_case: Conviction in EU broadening needs stability in EGB spreads, and the US is the clearer venue for broadening.
